residualProvenanceConflictRecordedNotSco.what: The packet tells the participant, in capitals, 'IF YOU HAVE READ THAT EXPUNCTION COSTS $250 TO $500, THAT RANGE IS FROM THE REPEALED STATUTE AND THIS PACKET WILL NOT REPEAT IT', and the instructions repeat it as 'The $250-to-$500 range that circulates online comes from the repealed statute'. NO HELD RECORD SAYS THE RANGE COMES FROM ART. 102.006. The committed track registry says only that the packet does not quote 'the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable'. The compiled Texas profile attributes it to something else entirely: in filingDestinationRules, describing step 4 of this very route, it records 'File in a district court for the county of arrest or prosecution (Art. 55A.251). Pay the civil filing fee, which varies by county (often roughly $250-$500 for expunction in many counties; some are lower)'. That is a description of the COUNTY CIVIL FILING FEE — which is exactly the fee art. 102.0061(a) makes applicable in district court, the same fact and the same route, so A3 does not exclude it.
residualProvenanceConflictRecordedNotSco.whyItDoesNotFailTheObligation: A1 asks the route-specific record first, and the committed track registry directs the exclusion in terms. The obligation is met on limb one regardless: the fee rule is stated and sourced, the mandatory waiver is stated with its subsection, and the Rule 145 form ships.
residualProvenanceConflictRecordedNotSco.whatIsActuallyWrong: The provenance clause is an unsourced assertion printed to a participant, and it conflicts with the compiled profile. A reader who checks will find the range attached to county civil filing fees, not to art. 102.006, and will not be able to tell which record to believe.
residualProvenanceConflictRecordedNotSco.raisedNotDecided: Flagged for Captain rather than scored, in the shape A3 itself was raised. Two held records describe one figure differently and the packet picks a third description. Whether a lane may fail FEE_AND_WAIVER on a false provenance clause when the fee rule itself is right is a yardstick question, not a reading question, and this lane will not settle it alone.

perRouteTreatmentRecommendation.whyNotA: Treatment A needs the mandatory official form to be available AND participant-filed. Neither half holds. S.C. Code § 17-22-930 requires the applicant to obtain the mandatory blank expungement order form from the solicitor's office in the judicial circuit where the charge originated and makes that form mandatory to the exclusion of all other expungement forms; § 17-22-940(B)(1) makes assisting the applicant to complete it that office's own duty; § 17-22-940(E)(3) forbids any official allowing the applicant to take possession of the application during the process; and § 17-22-940(B)(7) has the solicitor, not the participant, file the signed order with the clerk and distribute certified copies. The memo's _participantDeliverableDetermination for this exact track states it in terms: 'LegalEase does not generate the solicitor's statutory expungement order and does not portray anything it generates as the participant's filing of that order', and 'every solicitor, attestor, clerk and judicial field remains outside-party work the package leaves blank.'
perRouteTreatmentRecommendation.whyNotC: Treatment C is confined to routes genuinely filed as court petitions. data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/SC.memo.json records destination.kind 'prosecutor' for this track, and for eleven of its twelve tracks; the single 'court' track in the whole memo is sc_17_22_950_summary, which this family does not serve. evidence.component: primary_filing (CR-65, Petition for Expungement of Records, Rev. 10/2024)

evidence.field: CR-65:Check Box2.0 and CR-65:Check Box2.1 — the two boxes of the sworn item '(3) (Select one of the following)': 'that I have not previously applied for an expungement in this or any other jurisdiction' / 'that I have previously filed for an expungement'
whatIsWrong: NEITHER BOX IS MARKED in the delivered bytes. Read at 150 dpi on all four fixtures (both families, canonical and boundary). This is a mandatory selection on a page headed 'I swear or affirm, under the penalty of perjury', so the packet is delivered with a required attestation unmade.

THE GUIDE NEVER TELLS THE PARTICIPANT TO MAKE IT. participant-instructions.md contains no occurrence of 'Select one', 'previously applied', 'previously filed' or 'pro se' in either family (case-insensitive grep, zero hits).

WORSE, THE GUIDE DIRECTS THE TWO DEPENDENT BLANKS UNCONDITIONALLY. Its 'Required before filing' section opens 'Fill every item below on both the canonical and boundary-style packet before filing' and then lists, as items 20 and 21, 'County where any previous expungement was filed' and 'Court case number of any previous expungement'. Those two blanks exist only on the SECOND branch of the unmade selection. A participant who has never sought an expungement and follows the instruction literally writes a county and a case number for a prior expungement that does not exist, on a page sworn under penalty of perjury, while the attestation that governs those two blanks stays empty.

The 'pro se (Not represented by an attorney)' box on the same page is also unmarked and also undisclosed, on a packet whose entire attorney block is refused as 'attorney-only; no representation fact is held'.
evidence.whyTheCountersCannotSeeIt: production-field-map.json classifies both boxes as refusals with reason 'A genuine participant election not determined by this route', refusalClass 'participant_sworn_narrative_or_legal_election', isSelectionControl true, routeDetermined false, and NO requiredBeforeFiling flag. completeness-contract.mjs makes PARTICIPANT_ELECTION_GENUINE an allowed disposition that — unlike REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING — carries no DISCLOSED condition, so writeGuides() never surfaces it and requiredOptionsMissing reads 0. The counter accepts the field map as its classification authority, which is the same blind spot FIX09 recorded.
evidence.positiveControlThatThisZeroIsReal: Marks DO render on these fixtures and this lane proved it twice on the same bytes before believing any absence: (1) C-10-CRIMINAL page 1 (PDF page 9) shows a visible tick in the 'STATE OF ALABAMA' caption box (field Check Box1.0) at 150 dpi; (2) al-felony-dwop-set CR-65 page 3 (PDF page 3) shows a visible tick against the dismissed-without-prejudice Section III ground (field Check Box10.3). notarization.howMuchWeightToGiveIt: This lane is deliberately NOT failing an obligation on this. CR-65 page 6's own printed face is a jurat — 'I swear or affirm, under the penalty of perjury', 'Sworn to and subscribed before me this ___ day of ___', 'Notary Public/Officer Authorized to Administer Oaths', '(Notary Public Only: My Commission Expires on ___)'. 'The source review does not state a notarization requirement' is not the same proposition as 'notarization is not required', and a repair that strips the direction could leave a participant filing an unsworn affidavit. This is reported so a human decides, not so a repair lane deletes a sentence.
notarization.whatIsUnambiguouslyWrong: The claim under test — that the guide no longer directs notarization — is FALSE as a matter of measurement, in three of the four Alabama guide files across these two families, and one of the three is a direction the repair under test introduced. notarization.forWhoeverResolvesIt: AL.memo.json rules.notarization is identical across all eight CR-65 tracks, so this is one decision for Alabama, not two. If the direction is correct, the memo should record the jurat on the form's own face as its ground. If it is not, four files need the sentence removed and FIX04's whatWasDone corrected.

SOURCE_IDENTITY.finding: THE MISSING DIGESTS WERE ADDED AND THEY DO RECOMPUTE — BUT ONE OF THEM IS A CURRENT HASH PRESENTED AS A BUILD-TIME BINDING, WITH NOTHING IN THE RECEIPT DISCLOSING THAT THE RECORD MOVED. The earlier verifier was right that the grounds carried no digest, and the repair did add SHA-256 to both. Walking pins BY SHAPE finds them under the path key `record` (not `path` or `pathInRepository`), which is why a key-blind walker reported this family as binding nothing. Both recompute from disk: NV.memo.json 113a9728...(312293) and legal-design-packet-set-manifests.json 6076f734...(3683419). THE DEFECT IS THE SECOND ONE. The receipt's bindingMethod — rewritten by this very repair — now reads 'each bound by exact SHA-256 over its committed bytes AT BUILD TIME'. The family was built at d6b594038 on 2026-09-01, where that record stood at 80d88d69...(3674510); it was still 713ed7ab...(3677644) at the later pagination fix a120d8bd5 on 2026-09-04; the pinned digest 6076f734... first exists at d798dc66b on 2026-09-04, AFTER both. So the sentence is false: nothing bound those bytes at build time because those bytes did not exist. And unlike its three siblings in this same cohort and same repair window, the receipt carries NEITHER an identityRefresh block (AR, OK, WA all have one) NOR an exactObject canonical digest (NC has two). A reader cannot tell from this receipt that the record moved at all. THE SUBSTANCE IS SOUND AND I PROVED IT — the bound anchor, packetSetId nv_seal_probation_family-set, is object-for-object IDENTICAL from the build blob at d6b594038 to the bytes on disk, and identical again from a120d8bd5. So this is not laundered content; it is an untrue provenance statement over content that happens to be unchanged, and the receipt itself contains no evidence of that fact. NV.memo.json's pin, by contrast, IS the build-time pin — unchanged at 113a9728... since d6b594038 — and is sound.

pinWalk.method: Pins were walked BY SHAPE, not by a known key. Any object carrying a 64-hex value under any of sha256 / sha256Exact / digest / sha / hash / sha256Digest / contentSha256 / sha256OfRecord / recordSha256, or a path-like string under any of pathInRepository / path / pathInPack / pathInArchive / recordPath / record / file / filePath / sourcePath / href / location / documentPath / recordFile, was collected wherever it sat in the tree.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: The memo records 'None is prescribed. The guide states no amount and instructs the participant to ask the clerk 'whether the clerk charges a filing fee (the sections prescribe none and this packet states no amount)'. It refuses to invent, which is the correct handling of an open question.

SERVICE.finding: Memo rules.service: 'The sections prescribe none... the Division is the body given the right to object, and whether the petition must be served is not established.' The guide tells the participant to ask the clerk 'whether the petition must be served on the Division of Parole and Probation or the prosecutor (the sections prescribe no service)'. SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: ONE OF THE TWELVE RECORDED STOP CONDITIONS IS HALF-DROPPED, AND THE DROPPED HALF IS THE SUBSTANTIVE ONE. NV.memo.json track nv_seal_probation_family carries twelve selfHelpStopConditions. Eleven are carried by the guide, several in paraphrase, which is fine. The twelfth reads 'Any pending charge, AND ANY CONVICTION DURING THE CLEAN PERIOD OTHER THAN A MINOR MOVING OR STANDING TRAFFIC VIOLATION.' The guide's final bullet carries only the first limb: 'any pending charge, offence-category question, or immigration question.' The intervening-conviction limb appears NOWHERE — not in the stop list, not elsewhere in participant-instructions.md, and not in the delivered pages. A case-insensitive search for 'convict' across the guide returns exactly one hit, in the unrelated sentence about whether the judgment of conviction was set aside; a search of the full extracted text of the canonical fixture returns hits only in the statutory recitals about the underlying conviction and the NRS 179.245 track. So a participant who picked up a new conviction inside the seven-year period is never told to stop.

missing: any conviction during the clean period other than a minor moving or standing traffic violation
evidence.exactRepair: Add the intervening-conviction limb to the final stop bullet, so it reads in the shape the memo records: 'any pending charge, and any conviction during the clean period other than a minor moving or standing traffic violation'.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding: SIX PAGES PER FIXTURE ARE PAGINATION OVERFLOW: five carry nothing but a wrapped route key, and on the sixth the petitioner's own contact block is broken across the page break — in the boundary fixture, mid-address. HOW THIS WAS MEASURED, AND WHY MY FIRST PASS MISSED IT. My first clipping check tested only whether a value is truncated or overflows its rule WITHIN a line, and on that test both fixtures are clean — every long boundary value is present verbatim and nothing collides. That test cannot see a value broken across a PAGE break. I only went looking because two earlier lanes had failed this obligation on this cohort (vf29/vf37 on Oklahoma, vf02 on Nevada) and a verifier does not get to overturn a finding it did not re-measure. The probe: for every page of every fixture, take the first non-blank line and flag it when it continues a contact block opened on the previous page (PRINTED NAME / MAILING ADDRESS / TELEPHONE / EMAIL) or is a bare postcode fragment following a MAILING ADDRESS; separately count non-whitespace characters per page and read every thin page rather than trusting a threshold. My first threshold of 200 characters would have MISSED the boundary fixture's split page at 216 characters, which is why every flagged page was then read, and the two decisive pages were also rendered at 150 dpi and looked at.

FILING_DESTINATION.finding: The instructions do not name the court the route names; they tell the participant to work the filing destination out themselves, and the one court they do name is specified differently from the record's.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.evidence: THE RECORD SETTLES THIS AND THE PACKET DENIES IT. THE RECORD SENTENCES, from the track registry rules and the packet-set manifest's participantActionRequired, identical in both: pay_fee -- 'County filing fees vary and are not established by statute. The legal review reports a range of roughly $132 to $215 across counties, with expungement petitions generally costing more than limited access petitions. No confirmed statewide schedule exists.' apply_fee_waiver -- 'In forma pauperis relief is available; the Court of Common Pleas Motion to Proceed In Forma Pauperis is published statewide', with conditionDescription 'Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.' THE DELIVERED SENTENCE, participant-instructions.md line 89, quoted whole: 'The filing fee and whether it can be waived, who must be served and by what method, and the addresses the petition is served on are not established in this repository. Ask the same clerk. An unsourced figure in a filing instruction would be worse than none.' And line 105: 'The fee-waiver motion (PA-IFP-CCP) is held as exact source evidence only. It is not generated into your packet and nothing on it is a blank on this filing. If you need a fee waiver, ask the clerk for the current form.' SIDE BY SIDE: the record says in forma pauperis relief IS available and the statewide motion IS published; the packet says whether the fee can be waived is 'not established in this repository' and sends the participant to the clerk for 'the current form' -- while this repository holds that exact statewide form, bound by exact SHA-256 in this family's own source-receipt.json at b1255ef0...(760989 bytes) and resolved by content hash in this container. The record's caution about the AMOUNT ('no confirmed statewide schedule exists', 'roughly $132 to $215') is a reason to name no figure, which the packet's last sentence defends well; it is not a reason to tell a participant that the availability of a waiver is unknown when the controlling record says it is available. WHETHER THE RECORD IS OPEN: it is not. The wave-2 return at 677700997 blocked this obligation as MISSING_ARTIFACT_SPECIFIC_APPROVAL_INPUT on the finding 'County filing fees vary, no confirmed statewide schedule exists, and conditional use of the IFP motion requires participant/local confirmation. The exact fee/waiver branch cannot be resolved from the controlling record.' On the record as it now stands that premise does not hold: the branch is resolved and its condition is the participant's own election, stated in the manifest as 'Applies only where the participant seeks to proceed in forma pauperis.' A branch conditioned on a participant's choice is a settled treatment, not an open legal question.
FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: The record settles the fee and waiver treatment and the packet contradicts it. This is a packet defect a repair lane can fix, not an open legal input -- which is the answer this read was sent to get, and it resolves the wave-2 block in the direction of repair rather than of approval.

SERVICE.evidence: The same delivered sentence denies the same settled record. THE RECORD: rules.service 'Service on the attorney for the Commonwealth concurrently with filing, per Pa.R.Crim.P. 790'; serve_party the same words; rules.notice 'A copy of the petition is served on the attorney for the Commonwealth concurrently with filing. Within 60 days after service the attorney for the Commonwealth shall file a consent or objection to the petition or take no action.' THE PINNED FORM ITSELF prints, on the delivered petition page in every fixture: 'When this petition is filed with the Clerk of Courts, the petitioner shall serve a copy upon the attorney for the Commonwealth.' THE PACKET: participant-instructions.md line 89 says 'who must be served and by what method, and the addresses the petition is served on are not established in this repository'. A case-insensitive search of the whole guide returns 0 occurrences of 'Commonwealth'. The only service words in the file are two instructions not to fill service certificates until service has occurred. So the packet tells the participant that who must be served is unknown, on a page whose own printed text names the person to be served, and the record names the method (concurrently with filing) and the consequence (a 60-day consent-or-objection window) as well.
SERVICE.finding: Who must be served and how is stated by the record and by the form, and the packet's instructions deny that it is established. This is the second half of the same defective sentence.

SELF_HELP_STOP.evidence: The registry records seven selfHelpBoundaries for track pa_790_nonconviction and the guide carries three.
